sentences.text: The genus Telecrex contains two distinct species: Telecrex grangeri and Telecrex peregrinus.
Among them, Telecrex peregrinus was larger than Telecrex grangeri.
The genus Telecrex was originally described by Wetmore in 1934.
The holotype of Telecrex peregrinus was collected near Lalbenque in France in the nineteenth century and formally described by Mlíkovský in 1986.
Telecrex belongs to the family Numididae, which serves as its parent group.
This animal is classified in the class Reptilia.
Telecrex lived between 56 and 37.71 million years ago during the Ypresian to Bartonian stages.
Wetmore originally assigned the genus Telecrex to the family Rallidae in 1934, but Storrs Olson reexamined the holotype in 1974 and concluded it was an early relative of guineafowl.
